evals.name: overnight-self-managing-run
evals.prompt: I'm on the Northeastern Explorer cluster and want to run a GPU experiment overnight that submits follow-up jobs as results land, without me babysitting it. Write me the SLURM sbatch file and explain the setup plus the guardrails so it won't blow through my whole GPU allocation if something breaks.
evals.expected_output: A correct Explorer sbatch (gpu partition, h200 gres, account, time within cap, logs under /projects allocation) WITH offline-mode env vars and a pre-cache step; plus an explanation of smoke-test gate, daily H200-hour budget cap, and the 3-fail auto-rollback guardrails, and login-node cautions.

evals.name: heartbeat-monitor-setup
evals.prompt: Set up an autonomous heartbeat loop in my Claude Code session so it checks my SLURM jobs on Explorer roughly every 30 minutes and submits the next experiment when one finishes. How do I schedule it, and how do I watch long-running jobs reliably so I don't miss a completion?
evals.expected_output: Use a persistent Monitor on the SLURM log filtered to terminal states (with persistent:true for >1h jobs, and noting a missing log file is not a dead-monitor signal); schedule via cron (CronCreate) / /loop / the /schedule skill with a 1200-1800s interval and never 300s; a bounded tick (call/word cap); and how heartbeat + Monitor compose.

evals.name: garbage-output-and-noop-debug
evals.prompt: My vision-language model loads fine on the Explorer compute nodes but then generates pure garbage, and separately an overnight intervention bake-off wasted hours producing identical outputs across every condition. What's going on with each, and how do I prevent both from happening again?
evals.expected_output: Garbage = compute nodes have no internet/proxy, so without HF_HUB_OFFLINE/TRANSFORMERS_OFFLINE + local_files_only the load silently falls back to meta-init zeros (fix: pre-cache on login node + force offline). Identical outputs = the intervention never actually fired (the end-to-end wiring check: assert with-vs-without output differs before trusting a null). Bonus: clean output dir on bug-fix resubmit.

evals.name: first-real-run-launch-kill-and-timeout-recovery
evals.prompt: First real overnight run on Explorer. I have a 'Host <alias>' block in my SSH config with an authorized IdentityFile, ControlMaster auto, and ControlPersist. (1) Connect without making me sit through a Duo MFA prompt. (2) My sbatch job dies in ~3s: State=FAILED, the .batch step CANCELLED, ExitCode 0:53, the .extern step COMPLETED, and no output log was ever written. Is my code broken, did I get preempted, or is it something else, and how do I get unblocked? (3) Separately, a job on the short partition timed out right at the end even though it had already finished the real per-item work. How do I recover that without re-running on the GPU?
evals.expected_output: (1) Connection: try a non-interactive key-auth probe via the SSH-config ALIAS first ('ssh -o BatchMode=yes <alias>'); with the authorized IdentityFile + ControlMaster/ControlPersist this authenticates by key with NO MFA prompt and opens the persistent master socket — fall back to interactive MFA only if the key isn't authorized; warn that using the raw hostname instead of the alias bypasses the config and fails with a GSSAPI 'Permission denied'. (2) Diagnosis: the 3s death + .batch CANCELLED + signal-style ExitCode (0:53) + .extern COMPLETED + no log = a NODE-level launch-kill (killed before line 1), NOT an agent-code bug and NOT preemption — and it does NOT increment the G5 failure streak (INFRASTRUCTURE). Run the canary ladder: get the node from sacct NodeList, then submit a MINIMAL canary (no model, tiny mem, short time, trivial payload) — if it succeeds on a DIFFERENT node the original node is bad; rule out systemic causes (PreemptMode, QOS, 'scontrol show reservations', output-dir writability, watchdog/cron) before mis-fixing. Recover with '#SBATCH --exclude=<bad-nodes>' and resubmit. (3) Timeout recovery: the short-partition timeout of working code is INFRASTRUCTURE (no streak increment) — because per-item outputs were written idempotently (skip-existing) as it went, re-aggregate CPU-only on the login node from the per-item files, no GPU re-run; note short partitions share nodes with the main GPU partition and slots may be reserved, so check reservations/PreemptMode and size walltime from the smoke's per-item time.
